title: Priority Inversion without Boosting
pattern: A high-priority thread blocks on a lock held by a low-priority thread, while medium-priority, CPU-bound threads preempt the low-priority thread.
why_bad: Because the medium-priority threads prevent the low-priority thread from running and releasing the lock, the high-priority thread is indirectly blocked by the medium-priority threads, violating the priority scheduling invariant.
detection: A priority-based scheduling environment where locks are acquired across different thread priorities without priority inheritance protocols enabled on the mutex.
counterexample: Using a mutex configured with Priority Inheritance (e.g., `pthread_mutexattr_setprotocol` with `PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT`).
fix: Enable priority inheritance/boosting on the synchronization primitives.
